correctness.rationale: The exact finite-domain proof enumerates all 3^11=177147 inputs under the explicitly sourced Herschel adjacency and each standard local rule. Functional-graph indegree peeling and reverse propagation derive every first-entry time and least eventual period. A separately implemented C++ Floyd algorithm independently resolves each of the same 177147 configurations and agrees on every histogram cell, common period basin and recurrent state. Source scripts were run from the package paths, returning HERSCHEL_EXHAUSTIVE_OK and HERSCHEL_FLOYD_OK. The special sets and 8-/10-step maxima are checked exhaustively; no infinite-domain claim is made.

originality.rationale: A natural finite eleven-vertex irregular polyhedral graph has a pointwise equality of eventual least periods between CCA and GHM for all 177147 common starts, but 4752 versus 1200 primitive-four periodic configurations and distinct exact entrance clocks (8 vs 10). The published general period-divisibility theorem implies only p_H|p_C, not equality. Published biclique equality concerns a different family; published Petersen and Heawood cases exhibit period-halving failures. Independently read sources on model synchronization, maximum-walk activity, and geometric graph definition do not state the matched Herschel census. Novelty is best-knowledge and historical priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: No historical-priority guarantee against unpublished, unindexed, or otherwise inaccessible exact Herschel functional-graph enumerations.
Full reference paper appendices beyond specifically relevant inspected portions were not exhaustively read; available broad theorems do not assert the particular finite equality.
Complete finite exhaustive calculations are independently programmed, but independent external peer audit has not occurred.

value.rationale: The canonical smallest non-Hamiltonian polyhedral Herschel graph is a natural sparse irregular network for testing whether general CCA/GHM synchronization and divisibility sharpen to exact period equivalence. Complete period-basin coincidence despite almost fourfold difference in immediate four-period states (4752 versus 1200) and different worst transients is a motivated, exact whole-network invariant unavailable from broad qualitative criteria. Published Petersen/Heawood examples show real mathematical sensitivity of pointwise period equality to graph geometry. It is an exact natural finite classification, not arbitrary partial enumeration or parameter substitution.
